title: The request to write knob values
description: Writes the values a running sketch declared. Any number of them can go in one call. Placed atomically as ADR-0018 decision 3 requires, and id changes with every request. Within one request they are processed in name order, so writing the same name twice leaves the later one standing.

id.description: This request's identifier. The reply echoes it back. An id already answered is not processed again, even after the sketch relaunches: the answer left in the reply is the record. Do not reuse an id while the facet remains. **This includes a request that could not be read**: once it is answered, fixing it and placing it again under the same id is not processed — place the fixed request with a new id.

values.description: The values to write. **Only the keys listed for an entry are read**: a key beside them, such as min, is not read, and the request is answered without any note of it (the reply carries no warnings; a misspelt key in place of a required one is a missing field, so it is rejected). **Whatever does not go in appears in the reply's rejected, with a reason** — an unknown name, a type that differs, a value outside the choices, and **a write that cannot be read at all** (an unknown type, a value of the wrong shape, a number too large to read such as 1e400): none of them is dropped in silence, and the other writes in the same request still go in. **A request whose id can be read is always answered**: a values that is missing, null or not an array is answered with one rejected entry that has an empty name and typeMismatch, and nothing is written. A request whose id cannot be read (an id that is missing or not a string, or text that is not JSON, including JSON cut off part way) is answered with nothing, and a request whose id was already answered is not processed again (see id).

name.description: The name as it was declared. It can be looked up in the reply's params.

type.description: The value's type. **Written next to the value**, because JSON's number representation alone cannot tell a real from an integer, and an array alone cannot tell two components from three. A type other than the declared one is refused as typeMismatch.

value.description: The value. float and int are numbers, bool is a boolean, string is text, color is a tuple with red, green, blue and alpha (premultiplied, in the working space), and vec2 and vec3 are arrays of components.
